The simultaneous use of a neuroendoscope during VPS (Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt) procedures does not appear to increase the risk of surgical infection. A study found that this technique did not result in an increased incidence of post-operative infections.

In fact, the study suggests that using an endoscope during these procedures may actually be beneficial and can help reduce the risk of complications associated with VPS surgery. This is because the neuroendoscope allows for a more precise and detailed examination of the surgical site, which can help identify any potential issues or problems early on.

It's worth noting that this study was conducted in a specific population (obese individuals) and may not be applicable to all patients undergoing VPS surgery. However, the results suggest that this technique may be beneficial for certain types of surgeries and patient populations.

In summary, the use of a neuroendoscope during VPS procedures does not appear to increase the risk of surgical infection, but it can help reduce complications associated with the procedure.
